en: Mayon Volcano in Albay is renowned for its nearly perfect symmetrical cone shape among all active volcanoes in the Philippines.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, flowing northward through the Cagayan Valley into the Babuyan Channel.
Laguna de Bay in Luzon is the largest lake in the Philippines, covering a massive surface area of about 911 square kilometers.
Mount Apo in Davao is the highest mountain in the Philippines, reaching an elevation of 2,954 meters above sea level.
The critically endangered Philippine eagle primarily lives in the mountainous rainforests of the island of Mindanao and parts of Luzon.
The Bicol Region is the top producer of abaca, a native banana plant whose strong fibers are used to make ropes.
Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea is a protected marine sanctuary known for its rich coral reef biodiversity.
The Visayas is a central island group in the Philippines surrounded by the Visayan Sea, Sibuyan Sea, and the Camotes Sea.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park in Palawan features an eight-kilometer navigable underground river that flows directly into the sea.
Taal Volcano in Batangas features a main crater lake situated on Volcano Island, which is located entirely inside Taal Lake.
The Philippines holds some of the largest global reserves of nickel, with major mining operations located in Surigao and Zambales.
The giant Rafflesia, which produces the largest individual flower on Earth, parasitically grows on specific vines in Luzon and Mindanao.
